UX Engine 2.0 is out today. It’s a plugin for Claude Code: 8 skills, 2 sub-agents and 4 commands that make it reason about interface decisions instead of guessing at them.

What’s new in 2.0:

design-system writes a DESIGN.md at your project root — tokens, component variants and voice, each value carrying the one-line reason it exists. Rule zero: it reads what your project already encodes before inventing anything. Tailwind config, CSS custom properties, token files, then your most reused component. Only the gaps go to a short interview. After that, a value outside the system is either an extension you approve — written down with its reason — or it gets flagged and replaced by the closest token. Silent invention is how drift starts.

visual-character forces one explicit decision per axis before any styled markup gets written. Type: where the contrast lives. Color: one signature, calibrated neutrals. Space: compression, then release. Finish: borders, or shadows, or flat planes, not all three. It doesn’t tell you which style to pick. It makes not picking illegal. And it deliberately contains no list of banned trends, because that list would age into the next default.

/restyle de-genericises a screen you already shipped. Diagnostic per axis first, then a visual refactor — logic, component structure and copy meaning untouched, delivered as a before and after.

The other six skills cover intent before code, information hierarchy, complete states, feedback and affordance, form UX, and a UX auditor. All of them read DESIGN.md when it exists, so structure and visual tokens pull in the same direction.

$79 instead of $99 with V2LAUNCH, until 7 August. Your licence includes twelve months of updates, so if you’re already on 1.0 this one costs you nothing.
